description: Update README.md to reflect the six features merged on 28/09 that are missing from the docs: Azure DevOps multi-SCM (#266), secrets moved to .env (#272), per-repo auto_dispatch/auto_merge config (#264/#275), gateway secret-path precedence (#263/#274), orphan-slot auto-deletion on Step 2 failure (#267/#273), and the release-engineering pipeline (#247/#271). Every claim MUST match the verified code, not just the issue summary. This is the primary README deliverable and is independent of FEAT-002 (steering files), so the two could be parallelized, but keep terminology identical across both.
steps: Read README.md fully first. Match the existing pt-BR house style (the repo docs DO use em dashes; keep them for consistency inside these files). Cross-reference docs/ARCHITECTURE.md and docs/RELEASE.md for terminology but do NOT edit those two files.

Azure DevOps / multi-SCM (#266): Add a short section (or extend 'Como funciona'/'Setup') documenting that the pipeline now supports GitHub AND Azure DevOps via a unified SCM factory. State the two configuration paths verified in flow/adapters/scm/factory.py: (a) explicit per-repo `scm: azure_devops` with `azure_org`/`azure_project`/`azure_repo` fields, and (b) automatic detection when a repo url/name starts with `dev.azure.com/` (see scm_config_from_repo_entry / _infer_scm_from_name). Mention the transport modules live under flow/adapters/scm/ (github.py re-exporting flow/adapters/github_transport.py; azure_devops.py using the Azure DevOps REST API with a PAT). Note ADO auth uses AZURE_DEVOPS_PAT (see .env.example). Do NOT invent class names — the code uses transport modules, not classes literally named GitHubTransport/AzureDevOpsTransport.

Secrets via .env (#272): Update the 'Segurança / privacidade' section (and the cron setup section as needed) to document that secrets no longer live in deployment.config.yaml — they now come from environment variables / .env (gitignored). Point to .env.example (which lists KIROCREW_WEBHOOK_TOKEN, KIROCREW_WEBHOOK_SECRET, AZURE_DEVOPS_PAT) and note deployment/.env.example is the equivalent template seeded into ~/.kiro/crew/crons/.env by install-cron.sh. Reflect config.example.yaml's own statement that secrets are NOT stored there. Reconcile the existing bullet that says secrets live in config.yaml.

Per-repo config (#264/#275): Update the squad-config example and the reviewer/auto-merge descriptions. The per-repo flags are now `auto_dispatch` and `auto_merge`, declarable inline under `repos:` (each item a map with `url` + optional `auto_dispatch`/`auto_merge`) or via legacy `repos_config:` (inline wins on conflict), per flow/config/squad.py and squads/example.yaml. In the '### Comportamento do reviewer' section, change the sentence that currently says `auto_merge_on_approve: true` in squad config drives the squash merge: describe it as the per-repo `auto_merge` flag (with the global fallback being workflow_params.auto_merge_on_approve). IMPORTANT: after this edit there must be NO remaining literal `auto_merge_on_approve` token in README.md (acceptance criterion). Also update Principle #3 which currently reads 'Auto-merge é opt-in por squad config (`auto_merge_on_approve: true`)' to reference per-repo `auto_merge`.

Fix secret path (#263/#274): In the 'Dispatch de sessões (webhook)' section, mention that the cron now reads the internal gateway secret from `~/.kiro/crew/run/gateway-{port}.secret` with precedence over `~/.kiro/crew/.local_secret` (and then ctx._secret as last resort), because .local_secret/ctx._secret go stale after a gateway restart and caused 403s. This matches deployment/deployment.py ~line 823.

Fix orphan slots (#267/#273): Add a short note (near 'Dispatch de sessões' or the cron/troubleshooting area) that when Step 2 (POST /api/chat) fails after Step 1 (POST /api/chat/slots) created the slot, the orphan slot is now deleted automatically (_delete_orphan_slot in deployment/deployment.py) so it no longer lingers as an empty 'New Session...' entry in the dashboard sidebar.

Release engineering (#247/#271): Add a 'Release' subsection (or extend the Roadmap/Desenvolvimento area) describing the .github/workflows/release.yml pipeline: python-semantic-release driven by conventional commits (feat->minor, fix->patch, breaking->major), triggered via workflow_run after CI passes on main, channels `latest` (auto-moved each release) and `stable` (manual promotion; app.json defaults to "channel": "stable"). Link to docs/RELEASE.md for the full policy. This should be consistent with the existing README note about flow-update-check / setup.onUpdate.
After edits, grep README.md for `auto_merge_on_approve` and confirm zero matches; grep for `Azure`, `.env`, `auto_dispatch`, `gateway-`, `release.yml` to confirm the new content is present.
acceptance_criteria: README.md documents Azure DevOps multi-SCM support with both the explicit `scm: azure_devops` config and automatic `dev.azure.com/` URL detection, referencing flow/adapters/scm/
README.md documents that secrets live in .env (gitignored), references .env.example, and no longer claims secrets live in deployment.config.yaml
README.md documents per-repo `auto_dispatch`/`auto_merge` (inline `repos:` and legacy `repos_config:`) and contains ZERO occurrences of the token `auto_merge_on_approve`
README.md 'Dispatch de sessões' mentions the `~/.kiro/crew/run/gateway-{port}.secret` precedence over `.local_secret`
README.md mentions automatic orphan-slot deletion when Step 2 dispatch fails
README.md has a release-engineering section covering release.yml, python-semantic-release, latest/stable channels, and links docs/RELEASE.md
docs/ARCHITECTURE.md and docs/RELEASE.md are NOT modified
verification: Run: grep -n 'auto_merge_on_approve' README.md  → expect no matches
Run: grep -nE 'Azure|scm_provider|scm: azure_devops|dev.azure.com|auto_dispatch|auto_merge|gateway-|release.yml|.env.example' README.md → expect the new content present
Run: git diff --stat -- docs/ARCHITECTURE.md docs/RELEASE.md → expect empty (unchanged)
Run the baseline test suite to confirm no code was touched: python3 -m pytest flow/tests/ --cov=flow --cov-fail-under=75
findings:
Updated README.md only (commit 8efab6c, docs:). All six gaps documented: (1) New '### Multi-SCM — GitHub e Azure DevOps' subsection under 'Como funciona'. IMPORTANT DEVIATION FROM ISSUE TEXT: the issue said `scm_provider: azure_devops`, but the ACTUAL verified code key in flow/adapters/scm/factory.py (ScmRepoConfig / scm_config_from_repo_entry) is `scm: azure_devops` with azure_org/azure_project/azure_repo fields — documented the real key. Auto-detection via _infer_scm_from_name when name/url starts with dev.azure.com/. Described transport MODULES (flow/adapters/scm/github.py re-exporting github_transport.py; azure_devops.py REST+PAT) — did NOT invent GitHubTransport/AzureDevOpsTransport class names. (2) Secrets in .env: rewrote 'Segurança / privacidade' to state secrets do NOT live in deployment.config.yaml; they come from .env (KIROCREW_WEBHOOK_TOKEN, KIROCREW_WEBHOOK_SECRET, AZURE_DEVOPS_PAT); referenced .env.example and deployment/.env.example seeded by install-cron.sh. Also updated the install-cron.sh setup note. (3) Per-repo config: added 'Config por repo' callout in Setup with inline repos: (url + auto_dispatch/auto_merge) and legacy repos_config: (inline wins); updated Principle #3 and the reviewer section. ZERO occurrences of literal token `auto_merge_on_approve` remain in README.md (verified by grep) — reviewer section now says 'flag global de auto-merge do workflow_params'. (4) Secret path precedence added to 'Dispatch de sessões (webhook)': ~/.kiro/crew/run/gateway-{port}.secret > .local_secret > ctx._secret (deployment.py ~line 823). (5) Orphan-slot auto-deletion (_delete_orphan_slot) note added to same section. (6) New '## Release' section: python-semantic-release, release.yml triggered by workflow_run after CI success, latest (auto) / stable (manual) channels, app.json channel:stable, links docs/RELEASE.md. VERIFICATION: grep auto_merge_on_approve → empty; new-content grep present; git diff --stat docs/ARCHITECTURE.md docs/RELEASE.md → empty (untouched). ENVIRONMENT NOTE: host default python3 is 3.9 but project requires >=3.12; used python3.12 (at /usr/bin/python3.12) with `pip install -e .[dev]` then pytest. Test suite: 932 passed, 1 skipped, coverage 86.67% (>=75 floor met). TWO PRE-EXISTING FAILURES unrelated to this docs change (confirmed via git stash on base commit 9dbe694): test_dispatch_webhook.py::TestOrphanSlotCleanup::test_delete_orphan_slot_chama_session_control_close and test_prompts_loader.py::TestRenderPromptFallback::test_template_corrompido_ilegivel_usa_fallback — both fail identically without my change.

SEMANTIC-REVIEW ITERATION 1 (2026-09-29-020332-review.md, verdict NEEDS_CHANGES) — addressed 2 of the 3 README-related findings: (1) SCM factory not wired to squad/cron pipeline + name:/url: schema inconsistency: confirmed in code — flow/config/squad.py `_normalize_repos` reads only `url` (required) + `auto_dispatch`/`auto_merge` from `repos:` map entries and silently drops `scm`/`azure_*`; `ScmTransportFactory`/`scm_config_from_repo_entry` have NO callers outside flow/tests/ (verified by grep across executor/scan/deployment). Added a 'Estado de integracao' caveat in the Multi-SCM section stating the factory is a standalone adapter not yet consumed by the cron pipeline (transport in production is still GitHub), and that the name/scm/azure_* example describes the factory's ScmRepoConfig schema, NOT a live repos: entry. Also added an 'Atencao ao schema' note in the 'Config por repo' callout distinguishing the url: (loader) schema from the name: (factory) schema, and pointed the cross-link to the real #1-configure-a-squad anchor. (2) perf missing from release bumps: authoritative source is pyproject.toml [tool.semantic_release.commit_parser_options] patch_tags = [fix, perf] (NOT the stale root .releaserc.json). Updated the README Release paragraph to 'fix e perf geram patch' and cited pyproject.toml minor_tags/patch_tags as source of truth. NOTE: docs/RELEASE.md's own table also omits a perf row, but per constraints it must not be edited; README now matches authoritative pyproject.toml. (3) [see FEAT-002 findings] handled in arquitetura.md.
